mission: The resonance starts discordant — three traditions that have never combined. Ben, Sera, Kael join hands. Three notes that don't form a chord. It feels clumsy, unstable.
why_now: The resonance attempt's first moments — failure before success, earned difficulty
conflict: The three Force traditions resist combination — not because of hostility but because they're structurally incompatible. Jedi lattice-work, pre-Ruusan Jedi discipline, and Sith-trained Force manipulation operate on different frequencies.
turning_point: The discordance is overwhelming. Ben's instinct to control kicks in — he tries to lead, to harmonize the three notes by force of will. It doesn't work. His Lie, again: control as safety. The resonance resists being commanded.
opening_hook: Three hands linked. Three Force traditions touching. The sound of it — in the Force — is like three instruments playing in different keys simultaneously.
closing_hook: It's not working. The discordance is worsening. Veraine's ritual is building power. Torin's void is expanding. And the resonance is falling apart. Ben is trying too hard. He's leading when he should be listening.
emotional_trajectory: Determined attempt -> frustration at failure -> the recognition that control is the problem

stakes.personal: Ben's Lie making one last stand — his instinct to control sabotaging the resonance
stakes.interpersonal: Three people failing to harmonize because one of them is trying to dominate
stakes.external: The other two operations are succeeding while theirs fails

setting: Veranthos — mid-valley, hands linked, the Scar visible, the valley in chaos
sensory_details: The discordance — three Force textures clashing; Ben's instinct to control manifesting as Force pressure; Sera's tradition rigid and defined; Kael's tradition fluid and sharp; the three failing to combine; sweat, strain, the wound pressing
action_beats: Ben links hands with Sera and Kael and the three Force traditions collide — discordant, unstable, wrong
Ben tries to lead the resonance by force of will and feels it resist — his control instinct sabotaging the harmony
Sweat rolls down Ben's temples as the discordance worsens and the other two operations grow stronger around them
notes: The failure-before-success is essential. The resonance CAN'T work while Ben is trying to control it. His Lie making one last attempt. The breakthrough comes in Chapter 25 when he lets go.
